A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SA2C/SPPO research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–D support reliable comparison despite formatting changes and removal of the v1 checklist.

before.justification: V1 reports original Atari, MuJoCo/Box2D, and RLHF experiments, including numerical results in Section 5 and Appendix C.

after.justification: V3 retains those experiments and adds Qwen2 summarization results, hyperparameter sensitivity results, and training trajectories.

M1.justification: The reverse losses, symmetric objective, and continuous-action discretization remain unchanged. Equations 7–9 match; the added explanation of the beta–Z product and evaluation with Qwen2 do not alter the proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 22 Atari games, nine continuous-control environments, IMDB sentiment generation, and TL;DR summarization, including the same reward-noise conditions. Qwen2 adds a model configuration within the existing summarization task.

E2.justification: A2C/DA2C, PPO/DPPO, and SFT retain their roles in the corresponding comparisons. The new sensitivity and Qwen2 experiments compare against PPO; newly discussed related methods are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: V3 adds a Qwen2-0.5B LoRA evaluation with alpha=0.5 and beta values 0.2 and 20, plus an Atari sweep over five beta values under both noise conditions. These extend experimental configurations; the settings of the retained experiments remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V1 asserts broad hyperparameter robustness but reports selected settings. V3 adds a systematic five-value beta sensitivity analysis across Atari games (Table 11), training trajectories used to discuss learning failures (Figure 4), and a Qwen2 beta comparison with reported eventual performance collapse (Section 5.3). These substantially expand robustness evidence.

E5.justification: V3 introduces exclusion of extremely large improvements when estimating average percentage gains in Table 11, without specifying an exact exclusion rule. Existing seed counts and standard-error reporting are retained; the PDFs do not establish increased replication of the original experiments.

E6.justification: V3 adds Atari sensitivity averages ranging from 7.83–24.98% improvement without noise and 1.74–166.73% with noise, Qwen2 reward trajectories, and Atari learning curves. It also reports later Qwen2 performance drops beyond Figure 3’s displayed range. Matched original score tables, including Table 3 and Appendix C comparisons, retain their numerical values.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and gradient derivations in Sections 3–4 and Appendices A–B, including Equations 1–39, are retained. The beta–Z equivalence explanation restates an existing property of the loss rather than adding a substantive formal result.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that adapting reverse cross-entropy improves A2C/PPO robustness across control and RLHF tasks, especially for SPPO across hyperparameters. V3’s contribution bullets and additional experiments elaborate and support these existing claims without changing their central scope.

C2.justification: V3 expands the explanation involving PPO’s small minibatches versus A2C’s full-batch updates and distinguishes handling noise from deciding whether noise benefits exploration. It removes v1’s explicit concluding discussion of applicability to advantage-based algorithms and possible extensions to DQN/SAC.

D1.justification: V3 adds Qwen2/LoRA configuration information and reports training overhead of 10–20% for Atari and no increase for continuous-control or LLM tasks. Conversely, it removes v1’s explicit source-code repository URL, although Appendix C.1 still mentions repository scripts. Existing hardware and hyperparameter tables are largely retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds a focused discussion of perturbed-reward correction and potentially beneficial noise, citing Wang et al. (2018), Chen et al. (2024), Obando-Ceron et al. (2023), Schaul et al. (2022), and related work. This broadens RL-specific positioning while retaining the original SCE and RLHF framing.

P1.justification: V3 edits prose, adds introductory contribution bullets and Section 5.5, shortens the conclusion, and removes the reproducibility statement and NeurIPS checklist. The main section sequence and Appendices A–D remain recognizable, with much technical prose retained.

P2.justification: The main text changes from a single-column preprint to a two-column conference layout, with reformatted and relocated displays. V3 adds Figures 3–4 and Table 11, changes the illustrative rows in Table 1 while retaining the complete appendix results, and reformats and abbreviates the reward-error example table.

improvement.justification: The new sensitivity sweep and training curves strengthen evidence for previously asserted robustness, while the Qwen2 evaluation and expanded RL related work improve assessment of generality and positioning. These gains are tempered by removal of the explicit code link and applicability discussion, an underspecified exclusion rule for aggregate gains, and Qwen2 declines described beyond Figure 3’s plotted range.
